newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy cranks up sell-offs, sets third Eni offer.
newsitem.headline: Italy cranks up sell-offs, sets third Eni offer.

text.p: Italy started cranking up its privatisation programme on Thursday, saying it would sell a third tranche of energy giant ENI between June 23-27, while motorway firm Autostrade would be on offer this summer.

Treasury Director General Mario Draghi said in a Treasury document that the size of the latest tranche in ENI, the world's sixth-largest energy company, would be fixed on June 7 and published in newspapers the next day.

The maximum price for the sale offer will be set on June 21 and published the day after, while the definitive price will be fixed on June 28 and published the following day. Trading in the new shares will begin on July 1.
"We are confident that investors, both Italian as well as international, will welcome this new opportunity to invest in shares of a major Italian company," Draghi told a news conference later.
The Treasury still holds 69 percent of the group after two previous successful sales, one for about 16 percent last October and the first for 15 percent in November 1995.

Italian press reports have forecast that this time it is likely to sell between 15 and 17 percent and share analysts, who expect the latest chunk to prove another big success, believe ENI will follow its usual pattern of offering about 15 percent.
The Treasury is not expected to reduce its holding to below 51 percent this time around but is expected to offer a discount on the ENI share market price prevailing during the sale offer.
ENI shares, which closed on the Milan bourse before the Treasury announcement, ended 0.36 percent lower at 8,976 lire but in a stock market which finished one percent down overall.

Investors holding onto their shares for one year will get a bonus of one free share for every 10 held and the Treasury said it would not make a fresh offer of the energy giant's stock for more than six months after the June sale.

Meanwhile, Eni itself said in its sale prospectus that it expected 1997 net profits to show a further improvement on 1996 levels and pre-tax profit, based on the current trend, to be above last year's 8.79 trillion lire ($5.27 billion).
The Treasury is trying to push on with a list of key privatisations but some are proving troublesome -- like that of telecommunications giant Stet, due after many delays to take place in the autumn.

Draghi said, however, that the ministry planned to press ahead with selling motorway operating company Autostrade "before or during the summer." State industrial holding IRI owns 87 percent of Autostrade.
The government has already named Banca Commerciale Italiana and SBC Warburg as global co-ordinators for the sale, which will be in the form of a public offer and private negotiation.
